findings.claim: isAccessTokenId matcher reads the wrong offset (substring(3,5) instead of substring(4,6)) and its comparison is inverted (returns false on equality), so it accepts essentially any grant; the updated expectCodeToToken/expectDeviceCodeToToken/expectRefresh/expectAuthReqIdToToken assertions never verify the grant shortcut. A prefix shorter than 5 chars also throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of returning false.
findings.evidence: Encoded prefix layout is session(2)+tokenType(2)+grant(2), so grant is at [4,6). Index 3 is always 't' (rt/lt) and no tested grant shortcut starts with 't', so the inverted check never fires. Executed jshell repros of the verbatim matcher logic (scratch matcher_check.jsh, matcher_repro.jsh, ocr/matcher.jsh) print true for onrtcc:<uuid> expected 'ac', onrtna:<uuid> expected 'rt', ofltcc:<uuid> expected 'rt'. Fixing only the offset makes every correct token fail; both defects must be fixed together.
findings.reason: Executed repro by four seats; the integration tests give no evidence for the feature. Fix: if (!items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false; plus a length guard.

findings.claim: client_credentials tokens are encoded with grant 'na' instead of the registered 'cc', because this grant builds tokens via tokenManager.responseBuilder(...).generateAccessToken() and never sets Constants.GRANT_TYPE on the client session context. Same gap for UMA/permission grant ('pg' never emitted, AuthorizationTokenService.java:358) and V1/legacy token exchange (AbstractTokenExchangeProvider.java:410).
findings.evidence: grep -rn 'setAttribute(Constants.GRANT_TYPE' services/src/main lists only OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse, ROPC, TokenManager.refreshAccessToken, PreAuthorizedCodeGrantType, StandardTokenExchangeProvider. DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext falls back to UNKNOWN ('na'). Patch's own unit test uses 'trltcc:1234' as the client-credentials example, which production never emits. Reasoned; not run against a server. Test that would fail: in ClientCredentialsGrantTest/ServiceAccountTest assert oauth.verifyToken(accessToken).getId().substring(4,6) equals 'cc'.
findings.reason: Core feature intent (grant type in jti) is broken for a primary grant; cited call sites support it. Red test is the ClientCredentials jti assertion above; fix by setting Constants.GRANT_TYPE in ClientCredentialsGrantType, AuthorizationTokenService and AbstractTokenExchangeProvider before token generation.

findings.claim: Copy-paste slip: Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed") re-checks grantType, so rawTokenId is never null-checked and a null raw id encodes to e.g. 'onrtac:null'.
findings.evidence: Line text as quoted by all four seats; constructor already null-checks grantType on the preceding line.

findings.claim: getShortcut() is a new abstract method with no default; a custom OAuth2GrantTypeFactory compiled against the old interface throws AbstractMethodError in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit (server startup), and a null shortcut NPEs on ConcurrentHashMap.put.
findings.evidence: postInit iterates all grant factories and calls getShortcut(). All 10 in-repo implementers were updated (grep). Raised as Important by open-code-review, Minor by superpowers and mattpocock.
findings.reason: Severity normalised to Minor on source evidence: OAuth2GrantTypeSpi.isInternal() returns true (server-spi-private/.../OAuth2GrantTypeSpi.java:34-36), so third-party grant factories are unsupported. ponytail: add a null check in postInit if external grant factories become supported.

findings.claim: Javadoc says the shortcut is 'usually like 3-letters', but decoding (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:74) requires the prefix to be exactly 6 chars (2+2+2) and postInit only checks for duplicates, not length; a 3-letter shortcut encodes fine but produces IDs getTokenContextFromTokenId rejects with IllegalArgumentException.
findings.evidence: Javadoc text vs. length check in getTokenContextFromTokenId; encodeTokenId never validates length; postInit validation is the map-size duplicate check only.
findings.reason: Cheap: correct the javadoc to '2-letter' and assert shortcut length == 2 in postInit. Minor because getTokenContextFromTokenId has no production caller yet.

findings.claim: User-visible change to access-token jti and event token_id format (bare UUID -> '<ss><tt><gg>:<uuid>') has no upgrade/release note, breaching PR-CHECKLIST.md ('updates to release notes and upgrade guide if applicable').
findings.evidence: Patch touches nothing under docs/documentation/upgrading; consumers parsing jti as a UUID will break.
findings.reason: Documented standard breach with a real compatibility impact for token consumers; add an upgrade-guide note.

findings.claim: New unit test uses org.junit.Assert.assertEquals with actual and expected swapped, against docs/tests-development.md (prefer MatcherAssert.assertThat, avoid org.junit.Assert.*); failure messages would read backwards.
findings.evidence: docs/tests-development.md guidance; every assertion in the new test is Assert.assertEquals(actual, expected).
findings.reason: Documented standard; swapped arguments mislead on failure. Mechanical change.

findings.claim: Constants.GRANT_TYPE = OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE is a pure alias; the patch uses both names (OAuth2GrantType.Context reads OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE, grants/TokenManager write Constants.GRANT_TYPE).
findings.evidence: Constant definition in patch; mixed usage across OAuth2GrantType.java and the grant classes.
findings.reason: Advisory; deleting the alias removes a second name for one string. Non-blocking.

findings.claim: grantsToShortcuts duplicates sessionFactory.getProviderFactory(OAuth2GrantType.class, gt) with a hand-maintained, unsynchronised cache that can go stale on undeploy; the hot-deploy refresh path in getGrantTypeByShortcut adds entries without the duplicate-shortcut check postInit performs.
findings.evidence: Lines 42,68,76,79,106-137 per ponytail seat; superpowers seat noted the unsynchronised lazy refresh and missing hot-deploy collision check but set it aside.
findings.reason: Advisory over-engineering; no observed failure. ponytail: encode via getProviderFactory(...).getShortcut() and keep only the reverse map when this code is next touched.

findings.claim: Factory builds HashMaps for 3- and 4-value enums (SessionType, TokenType) where an enum static fromShortcut would do; the maps include UNKNOWN 'un' shortcuts so decode accepts 'ununna:x' which encodeTokenId refuses to encode.
findings.evidence: init() lines 50-61 and getters 98-104; encodeTokenId rejects UNKNOWN (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:337-342 per seat).
findings.reason: Advisory; decode has no production caller, asymmetry is harmless today. ponytail: move lookup onto the enums.

findings.claim: Context.grantType is captured from formParams at construction and not refreshed by setFormParams.
findings.evidence: No in-repo caller of setFormParams (open-code-review grep).
findings.reason: No runtime effect today. ponytail: derive grantType from formParams in setFormParams if a caller appears.

findings.claim: Public Context(Context) copy constructor removed from the SPI; API removal unrelated to the feature.
findings.evidence: Raised by open-code-review, superpowers and mattpocock (borderline); ponytail called it a good deletion.
findings.reason: grep shows the only Context construction site is TokenEndpoint.java:149 (no copy-constructor callers), and OAuth2GrantTypeSpi.isInternal() returns true, so no supported consumer breaks.

findings.claim: AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.getShouldUseLightweightToken is now invoked for every access token, dereferencing session.getContext().getClient(); a context without a client would NPE even when no mappers run, and it reads the requesting client rather than the token's client.
findings.evidence: Reasoned; no concrete null-client caller found. superpowers seat set aside the same concern because the call already runs in default protocol mappers on those paths.
findings.reason: Matches existing mapper semantics; no reproducible path. ponytail: settle with a test issuing a token from PolicyEvaluationService/KeycloakIdentity paths.

findings.claim: @Column(name="ID", length = 36) is now shorter than the new 43-char access-token ids.
findings.evidence: Liquibase column is VARCHAR(255) (jpa-changelog-26.0.0.xml:60), so no runtime failure; annotation is stale. File outside the patch.
findings.reason: Outside the patch, no runtime effect. ponytail: align annotation length with the schema when the entity is next touched.

findings.claim: Unrelated typo rename requestedAucienceClients -> requestedAudienceClients breaches CONTRIBUTING.md 'do not refactor code not directly related'.
findings.evidence: Patch lines rename a local variable in TokenManager.
findings.reason: Local-variable typo fix in a file the patch already modifies; zero behavioural or API impact, reverting it is pure churn.

findings.claim: Commit format breaches CONTRIBUTING.md: two commits instead of one, ee2491268a uses lowercase 'closes #37118', daffb05b5a has no issue link.
findings.reason: Process issue resolved by squashing at merge time; not a code change.
